text: The Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR) was established in 1962 under the Department of Atomic Energy to formulate the Indian space programme and organise space research in the country. The committee's mandate includes the development of sounding rocket technology, the establishment of a rocket launching facility, the coordination of space research activities across Indian institutions, and the representation of India in international space organisations. INCOSPAR operates on the principle that space technology must serve national development objectives, with particular emphasis on applications in communication, meteorology, and resource surveying.
source: INCOSPAR Founding Charter, Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India, 1962

text: The Physical Research Laboratory was founded in 1947 by Vikram Sarabhai in Ahmedabad with the primary objective of conducting research in cosmic rays and upper atmospheric physics. The laboratory has since expanded its scope to include space science, astronomy, planetary science, geosciences, and theoretical physics. PRL's research philosophy emphasises the integration of observational, experimental, and theoretical approaches. The laboratory maintains a network of cosmic ray monitoring stations across India and operates sounding rocket payloads for upper atmospheric research. PRL serves as the primary research institution feeding scientific talent and expertise into the Indian space programme.
source: PRL Institutional History Document, Physical Research Laboratory, 1967

text: The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) was established in 1963 near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, on the geomagnetic equator. The station's location is scientifically significant because it allows direct access to the equatorial ionosphere and the equatorial electrojet. TERLS facilities include a rocket assembly building, launch pads for sounding rockets, telemetry and tracking stations, a payload preparation laboratory, and range safety systems. Since its first launch in November 1963, TERLS has conducted hundreds of sounding rocket flights for Indian and international scientists, contributing to the global understanding of the upper atmosphere and near-Earth space environment.

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established on August 15, 1969, superseding the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR). ISRO's mandate is to develop space technology and its applications for national benefit. The organisation's immediate priorities include the development of the Satellite Launch Vehicle (SLV) for placing small satellites in low Earth orbit, the design and construction of the Aryabhata experimental satellite, the planning and execution of the Satellite Instructional Television Experiment (SITE), and the establishment of ground-based infrastructure for satellite operations. ISRO operates under the Department of Atomic Energy and reports to the Space Commission.
source: ISRO Foundation Document, Government of India, 1969

text: The Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIMA) was established in 1961 as a collaborative effort between the Government of India, the Government of Gujarat, and the Harvard Business School. Dr. Vikram Sarabhai played a pivotal role in its founding, serving as the first chairman of its Board of Governors. IIMA's founding philosophy was that India's economic development required not only scientific and technical talent but also world-class management capability. The curriculum was designed to combine rigorous analytical training with practical exposure to Indian business and development challenges. IIMA's case study method, adapted from Harvard, was modified to include cases drawn from Indian industry, agriculture, and public administration.

The Ahmedabad Textile Industry's Research Association (ATIRA) was established in 1947 to bring scientific research methods to India's largest traditional industry. Under the guidance of Vikram Sarabhai, ATIRA developed into a model of how industrial research can improve productivity, quality, and competitiveness without displacing workers or destroying traditional skills. ATIRA's research programmes cover fibre science, textile chemistry, weaving technology, quality control, and industrial engineering. The association also provides training programmes for textile workers, supervisors, and managers, and operates a testing and certification service used by textile mills across India.
source: ATIRA Annual Report and Institutional History, 1960

text: The Community Science Centre in Ahmedabad was established in 1966 by Dr. Vikram Sarabhai to promote scientific temper among the general public, with particular emphasis on children and youth. The centre features interactive exhibits, hands-on workshops, science demonstrations, and outreach programmes. It was conceived as a place where ordinary citizens could experience the excitement of scientific discovery and develop the habit of critical thinking. The centre's programming covers astronomy, physics, chemistry, biology, and technology, with exhibits designed to provoke curiosity and encourage experimentation rather than passive observation.

The Satellite Instructional Television Experiment (SITE) is a collaborative programme between ISRO and NASA designed to test the feasibility of using satellite broadcasting for mass education in rural India. The experiment will use NASA's ATS-6 satellite to broadcast educational television programmes directly to approximately 5,000 villages equipped with direct reception community television sets. The programming will cover agriculture, health, hygiene, family planning, and national integration. SITE is the largest sociological experiment ever conducted using satellite technology, and its results will inform the design of India's future domestic satellite communication system.
source: SITE Programme Document, ISRO-NASA Joint Planning Committee, 1970

text: The Darpana Academy of Performing Arts was co-founded by Vikram and Mrinalini Sarabhai in 1949 in Ahmedabad. The academy is dedicated to the preservation and promotion of Indian classical dance, music, theatre, and puppetry. Under Mrinalini Sarabhai's artistic direction, Darpana has become one of India's premier cultural institutions, training generations of classical dancers and contributing to the revival and renewal of traditional performing arts. Vikram Sarabhai saw Darpana as complementary to his scientific institutions, believing that a complete society requires both scientific understanding and artistic expression. The academy embodies the Sarabhai family's conviction that science and art are not opposed but deeply interconnected expressions of human creativity.

The Space Commission and the Department of Space were established to provide a dedicated administrative framework for India's space programme. Previously, space activities were administered under the Department of Atomic Energy. The creation of separate institutions reflects the growing scale and importance of the space programme. The Space Commission, chaired by Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, is responsible for formulating space policy, approving programmes and budgets, and coordinating space activities across government agencies. The Department of Space provides the administrative support for ISRO and other space organisations. This institutional restructuring gives the space programme the autonomy and the resources it needs to pursue its ambitious agenda.
source: Space Commission and Department of Space Founding Document, Government of India, 1972
